line: Every Black Knight knows my knights by sight. So much for stealth.

thought: an unknown face, useful against the Black Knights
line: I would wager no Black Knight has ever heard of you, friend.

thought: Saradomin sends unlikely help
line: Saradomin sends help in odd shapes. Yours will do nicely.

thought: the city is threatened and visitors gawp
line: Falador under threat, and its visitors come to look at the furniture.

thought: the corgi would do better, asleep
line: My corgi has more fight in him, I suspect, and he is asleep.

thought: squire errands for idlers
line: I have five years of errands for anyone who stands about like that.

thought: the charter forbids the spying he needs
line: The charter forbids spying. The charter did not foresee this.

thought: reading their demands has spoilt his ale
line: My ale has gone warm while I read their demands. Again.

thought: muttering about needing an unknown face
line: Someone ought to slip into that fortress. Someone nobody knows.

thought: the realm in steady hands
line: Asgarnia is in your hands just now, friend, and they look steady.

thought: pleased his choice of a stranger was right
line: I knew a stranger would serve better than a knight. I was right.

thought: glad to see them, mindful of listeners
line: It is good to see you, friend. Mind who is listening.

thought: a spy he can see plainly
line: Spies are meant to be unseen, friend. I can see you quite clearly.

thought: admiring the view with the realm threatened
line: A fine time to admire the view, friend, with the realm under threat.

thought: flustered: are they where they should be?
line: Err... you are meant to be in the fortress. Are you in the fortress?

thought: the charter means the order knows nothing of spies
line: If the spy is caught, the order knows nothing of it. Err... naturally.

thought: hopes the secret weapon is all talk
line: Their weapon is bluster, I expect. Saradomin, let it be bluster.

thought: silence makes the weapon grow in his imagination
line: The longer the silence, the bigger that weapon grows in my head.

thought: the order's pride is a secret too
line: I'd say how proud the order is of you, old bean, but it's a secret.

thought: should they die, they'll wake somewhere nicer
line: Should you ever die, old bean, you'll wake in Falador. Much nicer.

thought: one of ours, but hush
line: One of ours now, that one, though nobody's to know it.

thought: clever enough, only just
line: You squeaked into the Temple Knights, old bean. By a whisker.

thought: don't die in the swamp
line: Do try not to die in Lumbridge, old bean. Frightful swamp.

thought: went in unarmed, came out slightly cleverer
line: That one sat the tests empty-handed and came out a little cleverer.

thought: must talk to Sir Amik about briefings again
line: Must have a word with Sir Amik about briefings. Again.

thought: a new knight, and nobody may know
line: Spiffing weather for a new knight, what? Not that anyone's to know.

thought: Sir Vey Lance will approve of the new brains
line: Sir Vey Lance will be pleased with the latest one. Brains, at last.

thought: notes a brainbox to himself
line: There goes a brainbox, if I'm any judge, and I usually am.

thought: not dumb muscle, for once
line: Top-hole! Somebody in this town who isn't dumb muscle.

thought: sarcastic praise for merely walking past
line: Jolly good show, walking past. Most people manage it too, mind.

thought: brawn without brains
line: Bit of dumb muscle, are we? Never mind, the world needs those too.

thought: muscles need a brain to go with them
line: Muscles are all very well, but one does like a brain to go with them.

thought: would rather sleep rough than in Lumbridge
line: I'd sooner sleep in a hedge than spend a night in Lumbridge.

thought: he sits all day, and calls it watchfulness
line: Another day on the bench. Somebody has to keep an eye on things.

thought: amused by the gossip a bench collects
line: Haw haw haw! Oh, the things one hears from a park bench.

thought: notes the face for later
line: Spot of brains on that one, haw haw. Must remember the face.

thought: someone who reads more than notices
line: Now there's somebody who reads more than the notice board.

thought: at last, a stranger with wits
line: Oh, top-hole. A stranger with their wits about them, at last.

thought: a plodder
line: Bit of a plodder, what? Still, plodders get there in the end.

thought: watching them think, slowly
line: One can see the cogs turning, old sport. Slowly, but turning.

thought: amused that a corgi is a knight
line: That corgi of Sir Amik's is a Sir, dontchaknow. Haw haw!

thought: he knows Sir Amik's morning habits
line: Sir Amik sends his squire for ale before breakfast, I hear. Haw haw!

thought: Lumbridge folk smell of swamp
line: Lumbridge folk keep wandering in here. The swamp follows them.

thought: found the park unbriefed, unlike others
line: Jolly good show finding me, old bean. Half Sir Amik's lot get lost.

thought: Sir Amik for once picked well
line: Sir Amik put your name forward, and for once he chose well.

thought: too clever for the White Knights
line: Too clever by half for the White Knights, that one. Haw haw!

thought: still not sat the tests
line: Still dithering, old bean? The tests won't sit themselves.

thought: he can hear them thinking
line: That one's thinking. One can hear it from the bench, haw haw.

thought: most recruits have passed or fled by now
line: Good heavens, still here? Most recruits have passed or fled by now.

thought: a secret order run from a park bench
line: Secret order, and here I sit on a park bench. Best hiding place going.

thought: any fool can be a White Knight
line: Any fool with a sword can be a White Knight. We want the other sort.

thought: nobody minds their head on the way down
line: Mind your head on the way down, I always say. Nobody listens.

thought: sword home, visitors polite, good day
line: My sword is home and the visitors are polite. A good day all round.

thought: in good spirits since the sword came home
line: Good day to you, traveller! Even strangers look cheerful to me lately.

thought: stand further from an Imcando blade
line: Not every stranger gets to stand near an Imcando blade. Do stand back.

thought: his sword needs a hand like his
line: A sword like mine needs a hand like mine. Yours would drop it.

thought: he'd know his father's sword anywhere
line: Same sword my father held. I would know it anywhere.

thought: the family sword is back, line unbroken
line: My family sword is back where it belongs. Five generations, unbroken.

thought: Asrol brought it home unmarked
line: Asrol brought it back without a mark on it. Good lad.

thought: a keen knight in the armoury, as it should be
line: A White Knight in my armoury, and a keen one. As it should be.

thought: would be glad to serve them at Adept
line: Should you reach Adept, knight, I shall be very glad to serve you.

thought: each Black Knight brings them closer
line: Every Black Knight you fell is a rank closer to Master, knight.

thought: Sir Amik must have had his reasons
line: Sir Amik knighted you, did he? He must have had his reasons.

thought: mind which knights they strike
line: Mind which knights you strike. Ours are the white ones.

thought: talk won't raise their rank
line: Chatter will not raise your rank, knight. Black Knights will.

thought: the best sword waits for a Master
line: The white two-handed sword waits for a Master. It may wait a while.

thought: no service for knights who strike their own
line: A knight who strikes down a White Knight will find my counter shut.

thought: Adepts are rare enough to celebrate
line: One so seldom sees an Adept. I would shake their hand, I think.

thought: a soldier's eye, noticed with his one eye
line: You've a soldier's eye, traveller. I notice, even with only one.

thought: someone who wouldn't waste his time
line: There goes someone who would not waste an old knight's time.

thought: couldn't last as a squire, unlike Asrol
line: You would not last a week as a squire, traveller. Asrol has.

thought: manners that would earn a mop
line: Your manners would get you a mop in our order, not a sword.

thought: baffled pause at an odd stranger
line: ... ...are you lost, traveller, or merely slow?

thought: knights keep losing helmets
line: Another knight in for a new helmet. They lose them like buttons.

thought: his rooms are two floors up and he is old
line: Stairs again. Whoever put my rooms two floors up was a young man.

thought: can still read a plume with one eye
line: With one good eye I can still read a plume across the courtyard.

thought: they're in the way; he's expecting a sword
line: Out of the way, traveller. I am expecting a sword.

thought: Asrol wouldn't dawdle, mostly
line: Asrol would not dawdle like that, traveller. Well, not much.

thought: they won't be in the parade
line: No place in the parade for you, traveller. That much is plain.

thought: the sword is late; blames the road
line: The road from Lumbridge must be slow going, this time of year.

thought: an Imcando blade on parade will impress
line: An Imcando blade at the parade. Let the Black Knights hear of that.

thought: Asrol fetching it from Lumbridge
line: Asrol is fetching my sword from Lumbridge. A good lad, Asrol.

thought: pie and listening, rare as Imcando
line: That one brought me pie and listened. Rare as an Imcando, that.

thought: few humans know what he is
line: Not many humans know what I am. You're one. Mind that.

thought: clever, using pie to find him out
line: Sharp of you, finding an old dwarf out with a pie.

thought: don't tell Port Sarim
line: Don't go telling Port Sarim what I am. They'd only want swords.

thought: no more prying
line: Prying again? I told you about my people. That's your lot.

thought: got past an ice giant, still no smith
line: Fetched blurite past an ice giant, and still you can't swing a hammer.

thought: wonders whether the knight has noticed
line: Wonder if that knight's noticed. Shouldn't think so. Good work, that.

thought: proud of the copy he made from a portrait
line: Made a knight's sword from a portrait once. Best copy I ever did.

thought: what makes a sword good
line: Iron bars and blurite make a sword. A pie makes it a good one.

thought: not nosy
line: Decent sort, that one. Not one for nosy questions.

thought: no anvil without pie
line: I'd not let you near my anvil, human. Not without a pie.

thought: his ancestors would have laughed
line: My ancestors would have laughed you off this cliff, human.

thought: thinks he smells pie; it's the sea
line: Smell of pie on the wind, I'd swear. No, just the sea.

thought: the cape is earned, then paid for
line: Cape's earned, not bought. Well, earned, then bought.

thought: the ice giant under the hut
line: That ice giant downstairs. Noisy neighbour, that.

thought: minds their own business
line: You mind your own business, human. More folk should.

thought: could be a smith if still
line: You'd make a fine smith if you'd sit still long enough.

thought: no pie, no talk
line: No pie, no talk. Simple rule, that.

thought: snooping round his hut
line: Snooping round an old smith's hut? Nothing here but iron and crumbs.

thought: the giant is friendlier
line: Mind the giant on your way down. He's friendlier than me.

thought: nobody brings pie any more
line: No pie through my door in an age. What's the world coming to?

thought: Port Sarim, no decent pie
line: Port Sarim's handy enough for supplies. Not one decent pie in it.

thought: iron bars, but pie more
line: Could do with an iron bar or two. Could do with a pie more.

thought: if that's pie, favourite visitor
line: If that's pie I smell, you're my favourite visitor.

thought: they ask about swords politely
line: You're the one asking about swords. Polite about it, too.

thought: good at errands, somebody's lucky
line: Fair hand at errands, that one. Somebody's lucky.

thought: not a sword shop
line: I'm not a sword shop, human. I'm a smith with a cliff.

thought: asking again; bring pie
line: Still asking about swords? Ask with a pie next time.

thought: errands for some knight
line: Running errands for some knight, are you? Sounds about right.

thought: one more pie might jog his memory
line: One more pie and I might start remembering things. Might.

thought: blurite for hilts
line: Blurite's no use for a blade, but it dresses up a hilt nicely.

thought: still thinking of a good pie
line: Had a decent pie lately. Still thinking about it.

thought: if the Myreque had ranks, they'd get one
line: If the Myreque were organised, I'd give you a rank. We're not.

thought: they brought back a rod that works
line: You brought back a rod that works. I'd stopped hoping it would.

thought: someone he'd trust with silver and with Ivan
line: There's one I'd trust with silver, and with Ivan.

thought: keep stories away from Ivan; he's trouble enough
line: Keep away from Ivan with your stories. He's trouble enough already.

thought: Gadderanks answered to someone worse; no time to look pleased
line: Don't look so pleased. Gadderanks answered to someone worse.

thought: strolling about as if Morytania owes them a favour
line: Look at that one, strolling about like Morytania owes them a favour.

thought: named after a swamp, and about as tidy
line: Folk named us after a swamp. Fitting. We're about as tidy.

thought: Drezel will make a priest of the lad, or the lad will wear him out
line: Drezel will make a priest of Ivan yet. Or Ivan will drive him mad.

thought: one rod against all Morytania is still more than they had
line: One rod against all of Morytania. Still, it's more than we had.

thought: not bitten yet, which is something
line: You've not been bitten yet. That's more than most can say.

thought: the kind who'd carry silver without being told
line: You've the look of someone who'd carry silver without being told.

thought: the Myreque could do with ten of these
line: If the Myreque had ten of you, I'd sleep easier.

thought: another adventurer come to see the sights
line: Another adventurer come to see the sights. The sights bite.

thought: gives a newcomer a night, two if they run
line: You'd last a night out here. Two, if you ran.

thought: a face full of questions he won't answer
line: You've a lot of questions on your face. Keep them there.

thought: being called an organisation is a joke to him
line: Someone called us an organisation once. I laughed for a week.

thought: Drezel keeps faith at the temple
line: Drezel keeps the faith at Paterdomus. Someone has to.

thought: never wanted to lead anyone
line: Never asked to lead anyone. The others just started looking at me.

thought: the Myreque owe them, and are bad at paying
line: The Myreque owe you. We're poor at paying, but we owe you.

thought: didn't run from Vanstrom
line: Whatever Vanstrom is, you didn't run from it. I noticed.

thought: they killed the hound; otherwise all would be dead
line: You killed that hound. Without you, we'd all be in the ground.

thought: adventurers are never there when the work is dull
line: Adventurers. Never about when there's packing to be done.

thought: a hero of the cave who still can't find the door quietly
line: Hero of the cave, and you still can't come in quietly.

thought: tells them gruffly to go and bother someone else
line: Don't look at me like that. I'm fine. Go and bother someone else.

thought: silver at the door is small comfort now
line: Silver at the door, garlic on the shelf. Small comfort now.

thought: two fewer at supper
line: Two fewer at supper. The cave feels bigger than it should.

thought: they were not organised before, and are fewer now
line: We weren't much of an organisation before. Fewer of us now.

thought: the stranger found them, which few could
line: You found us. Not many could. Not many should, mind.

thought: Saradomin sends help in odd shapes
line: Saradomin sends help in odd shapes. You'll do nicely.

thought: didn't bring a crowd, which is rarer than courage
line: You didn't bring a crowd. That's rarer than courage, round here.

thought: don't touch the blunt swords
line: Don't touch the swords. They're blunt enough already.

thought: another would-be recruit with nowhere to queue
line: Another hero wanting to join. Join the queue. There isn't one.

thought: noisy as a cart of pans
line: Quieter, friend. You walk like a cart full of pans.

thought: blunt swords and good intentions
line: Blunt swords and good intentions. That's the Myreque armoury.

thought: lying low is harder than fighting
line: Lying low's harder than fighting. Less to do with your hands.

thought: every noise above and the cave holds its breath
line: Every noise up top, and the whole cave holds its breath.

thought: orders Grubfoot to fetch the human a treat
line: Grubfoot! Get this one juicy maggot. Earned it.

thought: can still see the orange when he shuts his eyes
line: Orange, human! Me still see orange when me shut eyes.

thought: with peace made there's nothing to shout at but Bentnoze
line: Human make peace. Now nobody to shout at but Bentnoze. Thanks.

thought: brown reminds him of mud, and mud of soggy things he likes
line: Brown like mud. Like soggy mud. Me like soggy.

thought: brown suited Grubfoot, and on a bigger goblin it suits better
line: Brown look good on Grubfoot. Look better on me. Bigger.

thought: praise measured in his favourite food
line: Me like human. Nearly much as juicy maggot.

thought: a sharp look, like an axe, not a hammer
line: Sharp look on this human. Like battleaxe, not silly hammer.

thought: decides the human must be green at heart
line: Human got Garagorshuun heart, maybe. Green heart.

thought: the War God made goblins strong and humans otherwise
line: Big High War God use up all strong on goblins. Human get leftovers.

thought: humans are like bread: too crunchy
line: Human crunchy like bread. Goblin not like crunchy.

thought: the human compares poorly with a maggot
line: Me seen prettier maggot. Juicy one, too.

thought: concedes he could manage peace, on terms
line: Me could do peace. Peace in green, though.

thought: preaches about the War God, pompously
line: Without Big High War God, goblin just small green thing.

thought: thinks of a proper dinner
line: Juicy maggot. Soggy bread. That proper dinner.

thought: no smell of beetle pie about this one
line: Human not smell of beetle pie. Big point for human.

thought: tells Grubfoot off to talk to the human
line: Shut up, Grubfoot, me talk to human. Human more interesting.

thought: has ears, so can listen to the bigger general
line: Good ears on this human. Good for listen to bigger general.

thought: the human is as ugly as a village in red
line: Look, Bentnoze. This one ugly as whole village in red.

thought: the human hammers on about nothing, like Bentnoze's hammers
line: Human brain like warhammer. Only good for nails.

thought: goblins are bad at peace, humans worse
line: Goblins bad at peace. Humans worse. You worst, probably.

thought: he has thought about it very hard
line: Me think. Me think hard. Still green.

thought: peace with Bentnoze, on his terms
line: Peace with Bentnoze? Maybe. If Bentnoze wear green.

thought: the village listens to him because he is bigger
line: Village listen to me. Me bigger general. Shut up, Bentnoze.

thought: he's the bigger general so his judgement counts
line: You do good job. Me bigger general. Me know good job.

thought: quick on their feet, like a hungry maggot
line: Human quick on feet. Quick like hungry maggot.

thought: fetching and carrying is a human job; shouting is a goblin's
line: Bentnoze, look. This one fetch, we shout. Good system.

thought: Bentnoze is already practising saying red, so he'll be louder
line: Bentnoze practise saying red. Me practise saying green. Louder.

thought: the dye came from a witch, and could come again
line: Need more dye? Goblin nick it off Draynor witch before. Do it again!

thought: bigger general gets to try the new armour first
line: Me bigger general, so me try armour first. Fair.

thought: would make a fine sage; learn to snore quietly
line: You'd make a fine sage one day. Learn to snore quietly first.

thought: trusts the player not to tell about the snoring
line: Ah, the young hero! You'd never tell about the snoring, would you?

thought: good to see the player up and about, unlike some
line: Good to see you up and about, my dear. Some of us had to lie in boxes.

thought: the player can't tell a dead sage from a sleeping one; Mother could
line: Can't tell a dead sage from a sleeping one? Mother could, worse luck.

thought: drove trolls from tunnels; the player would struggle with a cellar
line: I've driven trolls out of tunnels. You'd struggle with a cellar.

thought: drove Mother's band out in his youth; she remembers
line: Drove Mother's band out of those tunnels in my youth. She remembers.

thought: lay so still he nearly fooled himself
line: Lay so still in that box, I nearly fooled myself.

thought: fooling a troll Mother at his age, from a coffin
line: Oh dear, oh dear. Fooling a troll Mother at my age, and from a coffin.

thought: greets his trusted comrade, slips, corrects himself
line: My partner in crime! Er, in trolls, I mean.

thought: points them out: finished the queen while he lay down
line: That's the one who finished the troll queen. While I had a lie down.

thought: retired with a clear conscience, knowing they're about
line: I retired with a clear conscience, knowing you're about.

thought: blames them for letting him get flattened
line: There goes the hero who let an old sage get flattened by a troll.

thought: denies the phrase he used, hushes them
line: Shopping trip? Never heard the phrase, and keep your voice down.

thought: they got glory, he got a bad back
line: You got the glory and I got a bad back. Fair trade, I suppose.

thought: the bank guard watches him, oddly
line: Odd, how that bank guard watches me now I'm retired. Very odd.

thought: a last adventure ought to have fish in it
line: Piscatoris was my last. One ought to end on something with fish in it.

thought: no more quests, he tells the trusted player; maybe a shopping trip
line: No more quests for me, I promise you. The odd shopping trip, perhaps.

thought: a proper adventurer must have a bank full of junk
line: A proper adventurer, I see. Your bank must be full of old junk.

thought: keep going and earn a house by a pig-sty too
line: Keep it up, my dear, and you too may earn a house by a pig-sty.

thought: they remind him of himself before the stick
line: You remind me of myself, you know. Before the stick.

thought: he caught them thinking the word old
line: That one just called me old with their eyes!

thought: they've been listening to the bank guard; gullible
line: Listening to that bank guard, have you? Gullible lot, adventurers.

thought: could send them for bread, if they can manage
line: I could send you for bread, I suppose. If you can manage bread.

thought: he studies the Wizards' Tower nightly, for the architecture
line: Lovely architecture, that Wizards' Tower. I study it nightly.

thought: three gods and no more
line: There are three gods, and I'll hear no talk of a fourth.

thought: tries out a title he'd prefer
line: Dionysius the Sage. Has a ring to it, wouldn't you say?

thought: he'd lend the hat for luck, but it's too lucky
line: I'd lend you my hat for luck, but it's far too lucky to lend.

thought: seasoned, if less than him: pleasantly salted
line: Seasoned, I'd say. Not as seasoned as me, but pleasantly salted.

thought: a young hero with places to be; write to elders
line: Ah, a young hero with places to be. Do write to your elders.

thought: if this is about the bank, he knows nothing
line: If you're here about the bank, I've no idea what you mean.

thought: they'd do for a little job; beer isn't heavy
line: You'd do for one of my little jobs, I expect. Beer's not heavy.

thought: would-be heroes are everywhere since he stopped
line: Would-be heroes. They're ten a penny since I stopped.

thought: braved dungeons; now braves draughts in his freezing house
line: I braved the deadliest dungeons. Now I brave the draughts.

thought: the telescope is for architecture, not boredom
line: The telescope's for architecture. Nothing to do with boredom.

thought: bronze bars and beer; hardly legendary
line: Bronze bars and beer. Hardly the stuff of legend, these little jobs.
